claims.text: The initial catalyst is a nanoscale, fully equimolar PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution with a homogeneous alloy phase.
Pd content can be systematically reduced while overall metal loading, particle size, and morphology are held constant.
Reducing Pd content changes local atomic arrangements and surface ensemble effects.
Reducing Pd content shifts the d-band center of surface atoms relative to the equimolar catalyst.
The Pd-induced d-band-center shift changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and its oxidation intermediates.
Changes in adsorption energies alter ethanol-oxidation turnover frequency.
Changes in adsorption energies alter the ethanol-oxidation product distribution.
Reduced-Pd catalysts will exhibit a shifted d-band center relative to the fully equimolar baseline.
Reduced-Pd catalysts will exhibit changed ethanol or intermediate adsorption energies relative to the baseline.
Reduced-Pd catalysts will exhibit a changed turnover frequency, although the direction of change is unspecified.
Reduced-Pd catalysts will exhibit a modified product distribution during ethanol oxidation.
The proposed effects apply only over compositions that retain the solid-solution structure without significant changes in particle size or morphology.
The comparison baseline is fully equimolar PtPdRhRuIrOs tested under reaction conditions identical to those used for the reduced-Pd catalysts.
Electrochemical ethanol oxidation is to be conducted under controlled temperature, applied potential window, and electrolyte composition that preserve the solid-solution phase.

Failure of reduced Pd content to produce a statistically significant d-band-center shift, measurable adsorption-energy changes, and consistent catalytic-performance changes would falsify the proposed Pd-to-d-band mechanism.
